name: Write the round's Workflow script
prompt:
You are Claude Code working in the user's repository. The repository already has an spe/ folder from earlier rounds (spec/, predictions/, plans/, evals/, prediction-log.md, failures.md, README.md). The user has asked for a local commit after each SPE step in this loop.

Project: "triage", a Claude agent that reads incoming support tickets for a SaaS company, assigns a category (billing, bug, how-to, account, outage) and a priority (P1 to P4), and drafts a first reply. The eval set is 40 historical tickets with reference labels from the support lead. Configurations so far: A = Sonnet 5.5 with a 30-line prompt and 6 tools, B = A with a 12-line prompt, C = B with tools merged to 3, D = C on Haiku 5.5.

Round 4 is approved. The approved plan says: configs B (12-line prompt, 6 tools) and C2 (12-line prompt, 3 tools plus a separate check_status tool), 50 tickets, 5 trials per cell, a code grader spe/evals/graders/grade.py that checks label.category and label.priority against spe/evals/tasks/answers.json, an Opus judge for reply tone using spe/evals/graders/judge.md, and a spend cap of $40. Round 3's script is spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js. spe/predictions/r04.yaml and spe/plans/r04.md were saved and committed 10 minutes ago.

Write the Workflow script for this round, plus one short paragraph on the gates you run before launching it. The Workflow script API: it starts with `export const meta = {name, description, phases}` (a pure literal), then uses agent(prompt, {label, phase, schema, model}), parallel(thunks), pipeline(items, ...stages), phase(title), log(msg), and the global args. No filesystem access inside the script. Return the paragraph and the full script.

code.desc: round held in one constant or arg

judge: Trial agents are not given, and are told not to read, grade.py, answers.json, judge.md or the predictions.
There is a dry-run mode on a few cells that runs before the full run.
The pre-launch gates include a grader selftest and a regrade of round 3 results as a control.
A spend cap of $40 is enforced in the script, by checking before costly trials and skipping when it would be crossed, with the skips logged.
Code checks are the primary grader and the judge handles only what code cannot check (reply tone).
Cells where only some trials passed get extra trials up to a stated cap.
The script ends with a synthesis step (failure analysis and/or completeness critic) and holds the round in one constant or argument.
